title: Hypoxia promotes the generation of a versican-rich extracellular matrix by human coronary artery endothelial cells
projectDescription: • Exposure of endothelial cells (HCAECs) to hypoxia alters gene an protein expression • Genes and proteins related to endothelial dysfunction and activation are overexpressed • Hypoxia induces a versican-rich matrix with an altered glycosaminoglycan profile • This modified matrix perturbs cell adhesion but enhances proliferation and hyaluronan binding • Hypoxia upregulates oxidant formation and proteins related to inflammation
sampleProcessingProtocol: HCAECs were cultured in 6-well plates (5 x 104 cells/well) for 7 days at 20% or 1% O2. After 7 days, cells were lysed in 4% SDS with 10 mM tris(2-carbozyethyl)phosphine and 40 mM 2-chloroacetamide to reduce disulfides and subsequently alkylate thiols (70oC, 20 min). Protein concentrations were determined by tryptophan fluorescence spectroscopy using λex/em: 295/350 nm, and an estimated frequency of tryptophan in human proteins of 1.3%. Aliquots of protein extracts corresponding to 20 μg of protein were transferred to low-binding 96-well plates and digested following an automated, 96-well adapted PAC protocol [92]. Briefly, 100 μg of magnetic beads were added to the samples, followed by acetonitrile (70% v/v). After mixing, the solution was incubated for 20 min at 21oC. The plates were then placed in a magnetic rack, allowing the beads to separate for 1 min before the supernatant was aspirated. The beads were then washed three times (without release from the magnet) with 100% acetonitrile and once with 70% (v/v) ethanol. Then the plates were removed from the magnetic rack and the beads resuspended in 100 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (pH 8.5) containing trypsin (0.013 μg μL-1), corresponding to a final 1:50 ratio of enzyme to protein. Trypsin digestion occurred overnight at 37oC. The plate was placed back in the magnetic rack and beads were allowed to separate for 1 min. Half of the supernatant (containing peptides) was then transferred to a fresh low-binding plate, acidified, dried down by vacuum centrifugation and stored at -80oC until analysis by LC-MS/MS.  The remaining samples were pooled and fractionated to generate a project-specific library. In brief, 50 μg of peptides were fractioned using high-pH reverse-phase chromatography on a Kinetex 2.6 um EVO C18 100 Å, 150 x 1 mm column (Phenomenex) using a Dionex Ultimate RSLCnano system (Thermo Scientific) operating at 40 μL min-1. A 42-min step gradient from 5 to 60% solvent B (20 mM ammonium formate, pH 10, in 80% acetonitrile) and solvent A (20 mM ammonium formate in water) was used for separation. Fractions were collected every 60 seconds with concatenation into 12 final fractions. Fractionated samples were then dried down by vacuum centrifugation and stored at -80oC until analysis by LC-MS/MS.  Before analysis, peptide digests were reconstituted in 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid to a concentration of 0.2 μg μL-1.  The peptides were separated using a Dionex Ultimate RSLCnano system (Thermo Scientific) with an Aurora series reversed-phase C18 column (25 cm x 75 μm i.d., 1.6 μm C18, IonOpticks), maintained at 45oC, coupled to a timsTOF Pro (Bruker) operated in data-independent acquisition with parallel accumulation and serial fragmentation (DIA-PASEF) mode. Samples were eluted using a gradient consisting of 2-30% mobile phase B over 17 min, followed by washing and re-equilibration of the column. Mobile phase A was 0.1% (v/v) formic acid in water and B was 0.1 (v/v) formic acid in acetonitrile. In the DIA-PASEF mode, the mass spectrometer was operated in windows spanning 345-1201 m/z and 0.67-1.44 1/K0 [V s cm-2], which corresponds to an estimated cycle time of 1.16 s. DIA-PASEF windows and collision energy were also left to default with a base of 0.85 1/K0 [V s cm-2] set at 20 eV and 1.30 1/K0 [V s cm-2] set at 59 eV.
dataProcessingProtocol: All spectral data were processed in DIA-NN (version 1.8.1) [93]. A project-specific library was generated by searching fractionated DIA-PASEF against an in silico predicted spectral library of tryptic peptides from all reviewed Homo sapiens sequences in the UniProtKB protein database (UP000005640, downloaded 2023-01-19). The precursor charge range was restricted to 2-3 and 1 missed cleavage was allowed. Match-between-run (MBR) was disabled for spectral library generation. Quantitative DIA-PASEF files was processed using the project-specific library with MBR enabled. Mass accuracies were set to 15 ppm and scan window was set to 0 (automatic) for all analyses. Further data processing and analysis was then performed using the programming software R. First, the DIA-NN identifications were filtered at a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) threshold at both precursor and protein level, then precursor intensities were log2-transformed, normalized, and summarized into protein expression values with robust model-based summarization [94]. Peptides mapping to multiple proteins were summarized into groups of indistinguishable proteins, and the data was filtered for redundant protein groups and proteins only represented by a single peptide.
